artifacts.synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed Illiana Presbytery's decision to elevate his censures from indefinite suspension from office and from the Sacraments to excommunication and deposition, without any additional judicial process. The SJC sustained the appeal 21-1, holding that due process principles require some form of process before censure may be elevated, though the majority held that full de novo judicial process was not required; the sole dissent (RE Eggert) argued that Traditional Process under the BCO Rules of Discipline was required, and a concurring opinion (Sartorius) also argued for full BCO process.

artifacts.title: Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Matt Ruff complained that Nashville Presbytery failed to conduct an adequate BCO 31-2 investigation and to find a strong presumption of guilt against TE George Grant; the SJC sustained both complaints and remanded, finding the investigation record was incomplete and internally inconsistent, and that conduct described by the Presbytery's own Shepherding Committee as 'sin' required an explanation as to why no strong presumption of guilt existed.

artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Delhi Presbyterian Church complained that Louisiana Presbytery improperly assumed original jurisdiction over church member Mike Holland, barring him from the Lord's Table for contumacy after he was cited in SPLC reporting regarding Auburn Avenue Presbyterian Church. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that because Delhi Session had investigated and acted under BCO 31-2, Louisiana Presbytery lacked grounds to assume original jurisdiction under BCO 33-1, rendering its judgment against Holland a nullity; three dissenting opinions argued the SJC lacked appellate review of the jurisdiction question because no timely complaint was filed against the assumption of jurisdiction itself.

artifacts.title: Sung Keon Kim v. Korean Capital
artifacts.synopsis: TE Sung Keon Kim appealed a five-year suspension imposed after a Korean Capital Presbytery commission judged him guilty by a process that did not properly serve an indictment or preserve an adequate trial record. The SJC sustained the procedural challenge, found noncompliance with BCO 32 and 34, and remanded for a new trial conducted under those chapters.

artifacts.title: Conrad v. Central Carolina. [ M26G (1998): 122]. Not sustained 21-0
artifacts.synopsis: Central Carolina Presbytery did not act unconstitutionally in denying the complaint of Conrad, et al. against the Session of Prosperity Presbyterian Church. Although various actions taken by the parties were open to differing opinions and interpretations, the complainants failed to demonstrate any unconstitutional procedure or violations of the PCA Book of Church Order.
